title: Madhusmita Misra Named Pediatrics Chair at Washington University
headline: Madhusmita Misra Named Pediatrics Chair at Washington University
subheadline: The Indian-origin physician-scientist will lead the Edward Mallinckrodt Department of Pediatrics and serve as pediatrician-in-chief at St. Louis Children's Hospital from January 4, 2027.
body:
• Madhusmita Misra, MD, MPH, has been named chair of the Edward Mallinckrodt Department of Pediatrics at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis, WashU Medicine announced.
  • She will also serve as pediatrician-in-chief at St. Louis Children's Hospital, with the appointment beginning January 4, 2027.
  • Misra joins from the University of Virginia, where she is pediatrics chair and physician-in-chief of UVA Health Children's Hospital, after nearly 25 years at Massachusetts General Hospital.
  • Her research focuses on how nutritional and hormonal changes affect bone, metabolic health and brain function in children, adolescents and young adults.

Madhusmita Misra, a physician-scientist and nationally recognised leader in pediatric endocrinology, has been named chair of the Edward Mallinckrodt Department of Pediatrics at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis and pediatrician-in-chief at BJC HealthCare's St. Louis Children's Hospital. Her appointment begins January 4, 2027, the university announced.

Misra comes to WashU Medicine from the University of Virginia School of Medicine, where she serves as the Benjamin Armistead Shepherd Chair of Pediatrics and physician-in-chief at UVA Health Children's Hospital. She will succeed Mark Lowe, who has served as interim chair since April 2026, according to Becker's Hospital Review.

"Dr. Misra is a visionary academic leader who combines world-class research with a deep commitment to compassionate care and mentorship."

— Bruce D. Levy, Dean of WashU Medicine

A career built across three institutions

Before UVA, Misra spent close to 25 years at Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston, where she guided the Division of Pediatric Endocrinology in opening regional clinics, implementing a new electronic medical record system, building a comprehensive pediatric diabetes programme and establishing specialised care teams for children with rare genetic conditions, according to her UVA Health profile. She has held leadership roles in the Pediatric Endocrine Society, including its presidency.

Her path began in India. Misra earned her medical degree from S.C.B. Medical College at Utkal University and completed training in India before a pediatrics residency at Maimonides Medical Center in New York, a fellowship in pediatric endocrinology at Massachusetts General Hospital and a master's in public health from the Harvard School of Public Health. She has said she was inspired to pursue medicine by her great uncle, the first licensed pediatrician in their state in India.

Research and what's next

At UVA, Misra directs the Pediatric Endocrine-Neuroendocrine-Sports Endocrine Laboratory, where her programme examines how nutritional and hormonal changes affect bone, metabolic health and brain function across the weight spectrum — from anorexia nervosa and energy deficit in young female athletes to obesity — including work on bone consequences in children with autism and type 1 diabetes. "I look forward to listening, learning and working together to create the next chapter of excellence across all mission areas — always with children and families at the heart of all we do," Misra said.

For the diaspora's large cohort of Indian-trained physicians in US academic medicine, the appointment is a notable one: a doctor who began medical school in Odisha will lead pediatrics at one of America's top-ranked medical schools and its children's hospital from January 2027.
